reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Phase 03 correctly identified missing config validation but misunderstood the attack path. The SSZ type KzgCommitments = VariableList<KzgCommitment, U4096> enforces a compile-time maximum of 4096 commitments during deserialization. Blocks with >4096 commitments are rejected at the network layer (SSZ decode) before reaching the runtime check at block_verification.rs:885. The spec (Fulu beacon-chain SG-001 INV-003) requires max_blobs_per_block <= MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK, and this invariant is enforced by the SSZ type system, not config validation. Config values >4096 are accepted but ineffective—no consensus split or type-safety violation occurs because such blocks cannot exist in memory. The actual issue is UX/code quality (accepting unusable config values), not a security vulnerability. Per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE severity classification, this does not meet the threshold for Low (requires exploitable network impact on >=0.01% of nodes). Lighthouse deployment share is ~31% per scope, but this issue cannot cause any network impact because SSZ enforcement prevents exploitation.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Fulu beacon-chain SG-001 INV-003: All max_blobs_per_block values <= MAX_BLOB_COMMITMENTS_PER_BLOCK. This invariant is enforced by SSZ VariableList type constraint (U4096), not runtime validation.
